eventMetadata.context_description: NEA observational data from Singapore's Changi Airport climate station—the official reference for daily maximums—shows a peak of 32°C reached mid-afternoon on May 11, driving Polymarket's 99.9% implied probability for this outcome as showers spread across northern, eastern, and central areas, suppressing further solar heating under inter-monsoon conditions with light southwest winds. Fortnightly outlooks anticipated 33–35°C daily highs amid above-average rainfall, but real-time conditions including high humidity (60–95%) and afternoon thundery activity align with historical May patterns where sea breezes cap peaks around 32°C. A realistic challenge would require delayed showers allowing prolonged clear skies before sunset, though forecast models indicate minimal upside risk; final NEA daily review expected post-midnight.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight clustering in short-range weather models like ECMWF and GFS, with ensemble means projecting 21-22°C peak 2-meter temperatures at Istanbul Airport (LTBA), the market's NOAA resolution source. Recent 00Z and 12Z model runs show a cool northerly flow over the Marmara region moderating highs amid partial cloud cover and Black Sea sea-breeze influences, limiting afternoon insolation compared to climatological May averages near 21°C. Differentiating factors include subtle boundary-layer mixing variations and stratocumulus persistence, yielding a 0.5-1°C spread; 21°C leads due to conservative airport readings versus urban heat. Real-time airport observations will clarify by evening as peak heating occurs 2-4 PM local time.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket favors a 33°C high in Kuala Lumpur at 35% implied probability, edging out 32°C (26.5%) and 34°C (19.5%), driven by the Malaysian Meteorological Department's (METMalaysia) latest forecast of a 34°C maximum amid isolated afternoon thunderstorms on May 12. Recent heavy rain and thunderstorm warnings over the past 48 hours, including for May 11, have heightened expectations for convective cloud cover that could suppress peak heating—typically occurring 2-4 p.m.—to 32-33°C, as seen in similar May patterns at Kuala Lumpur International Airport station. Differentiating factors include thunderstorm onset timing: early development caps highs at 32-33°C via shading and downdrafts, while delays allow 34°C; high humidity near 80% and urban heat island effects add variability. Ensemble models and climatological May averages around 32°C underpin the tight clustering, with final observations resolving the market.

The China Meteorological Administration's latest guidance calls for thunderstorms on May 12 with a 30°C high—slightly trailing at 17%—following recent observed peaks of 30-31°C on May 10-11 despite partial cloudiness and showers. Key differentiators include timing of convective onset from an advancing frontal system, variable cloud cover suppressing or allowing urban heat island effects, and ensemble model spreads of 1-2°C across ECMWF and GFS runs. Updated CMA bulletins and Baiyun Airport observations expected later today could sharpen the outlook before resolution based on official station data.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA's extended weather outlook, updated as of May 11, forecasts a high temperature of 32°C in Manila on May 13 under partly cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers and a low 20% precipitation chance, driven by persistent easterlies funneling warm, humid air during the peak dry season. Recent observations show Metro Manila enduring extreme heat indices above 42°C—placing areas like NAIA in "danger" levels—amid actual air temperatures topping 36°C in nearby stations on May 10, though urban sea breezes have moderated peaks. May climatology averages 33-34°C highs with historical maxima near 38°C; traders anticipate daily forecast refinements from PAGASA, as short-range model consensus and local heat island effects could shift implied probabilities before official Quezon City station resolution.
